title: AI-based analyses of multi-center, multi-parametric quantitative MRI studies in brain tumor patients with the aim of optimizing diagnosis and treatment
summary: Magnetic resonance imaging is the standard way of examining brain tumors, but conventional scans have two important limitations. They often cannot tell which type of tumor is present, and after treatment they frequently cannot distinguish a tumor that is growing again from changes caused by the treatment itself. Both distinctions shape the choice of therapy. This study adds a specialized imaging technique to the routine head scan that patients undergo as part of their care. Rather than producing images alone, it measures properties of the tissue, such as its water content, and expresses them as numbers. This lengthens the scan by up to 15 minutes and requires no additional procedures, medication or contrast agent. The images and measurements are then analyzed, together with information on each patient’s disease and treatment, using artificial intelligence: computer programs that learn to recognize patterns in large amounts of data. The study will show whether this approach allows brain tumors to be characterized more accurately than is possible today. Thirteen university hospitals across Germany are taking part, and 621 patients are to be enrolled.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Clinical indication for brain MRI for diagnosis and treatment planning in suspected diffuse glioma or, in known diffuse glioma, to clarify the question of progression versus treatment-related changes (pseudoprogression). Written informed consent. Non-German-speaking persons may be included if they can be fully informed with the help of an interpreter.
Exclusion criteria:
Absolute contraindications to MRI (including contraindications to gadolinium-based contrast agents in clinical routine); inability to comply with an MRI examination or with the study-related prolongation of the examination; lack of capacity to consent.
